events.title: Basiliscus Seizes the Byzantine Throne
events.description: Basiliscus was crowned Emperor of the Byzantine Empire in a ceremony at the Hebdomon palace in Constantinople. He took power after Emperor Zeno was forced from the city.
events.significance: His short, turbulent reign shows how unstable imperial power was in the late Roman world, as the empire's eastern half struggled to hold itself together.

events.title: The Palermo Uprising Ignites Revolution
events.description: The people of Palermo in Sicily rose up against the Bourbon Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. The rebellion began on the birthday of the Bourbon king.
events.significance: It was the first of the 1848 revolutions that spread across Europe. It helped set off a wave of demands for constitutional government and national unity.

events.title: Rocky Mountain National Park Is Created
events.description: The U.S. Congress passed an act establishing Rocky Mountain National Park in Colorado. The act protected a landscape of high peaks, alpine lakes and wildlife.
events.significance: The park became one of the best-known protected areas in America. It marked a growing national commitment to conserving wild places.

events.title: Hattie Caraway Becomes the First Woman Elected to the U.S. Senate
events.description: Hattie W. Caraway of Arkansas won election to the United States Senate. She had first been appointed to fill the seat left by her late husband.
events.significance: Her victory was a milestone for women in American politics. It showed that women could win a Senate seat in their own right.

events.title: Tragedy at the Hajj in Mina
events.description: A stampede during the Stoning the Devil ritual on the final day of the Hajj in Mina, Saudi Arabia, killed at least 362 pilgrims.
events.significance: The disaster drew attention to the dangers of crowd control at one of the largest annual gatherings in the world. It contributed to later safety improvements at the site.
